name: Munitions Resupply Bay
desc: Carries %s/%s/%s/%s munitions, by hull size, and sends shuttles to top up the ballistic and missile ammo of friendly ships within %s/%s/%s/%s. A shuttle that's shot down loses its load, and the stock doesn't refill during a battle. Incompatible with the Boarding Shuttle Bay and Repair Tender Bay.
short: Supply shuttles refill nearby ships' ammo.

name: Boarding Shuttle Bay
desc: Launches waves of %s/%s/%s/%s shuttles, by hull size, each carrying %s marines, to board and capture enemy ships. One wave every %s seconds; marines on a shuttle that's shot down are lost. Incompatible with the Munitions Resupply Bay and Repair Tender Bay.
short: Marine shuttles board and capture enemy ships.

name: Repair Tender Bay
desc: Carries %s/%s/%s/%s repair drones and %s/%s/%s/%s spare parts, by hull size. The drones fix reactors, weapons, engines and armor (up to %s of its strength) on nearby friendly ships, using up parts. Drones that are shot down are lost, and the tender can't repair itself. Incompatible with the Munitions Resupply Bay and Boarding Shuttle Bay.
short: Repair drones fix nearby ships during battle.

name: Tug Rig
desc: Tows friendly ships that can't move to a Repair Dock, tender, Supply FOB or supply ship. The tug slows down while towing, to no less than %s of its speed. In RTS mode, select the tug and right-click the stranded ship.
short: Tows stranded ships to a Repair Dock, tender, FOB or supply ship.

name: Explosive Reactive Armor
desc: Reactive tiles over the armor: %s/%s/%s/%s charges per armor section, by hull size. A charge stops an HE missile outright or cuts an HE shell's damage by %s. An empty section reloads once, after %s seconds; after that it needs a tender or Repair Dock. The ship is %s less maneuverable.

name: Composite Armor Replacement
desc: Lighter composite plating: kinetic and HE hits do %s less damage, but armor is %s lower. The ship is %s faster and more maneuverable. Stacks with ERA (the stronger HE reduction applies) and Spall Lining.

name: Spall Lining
desc: A liner behind the armor that catches fragments from shells breaking through. Shells penetrate %s less well. The extra weight makes the ship %s less maneuverable. Stacks with Composite Armor Replacement and Explosive Reactive Armor.

name: TCO - Ship and Weapon Data
desc: A readout with no effect in battle. Shows TCO's numbers for this ship with its hullmods and skills applied: reactor power (capacity, regeneration and how long the weapons can keep firing) and, for each weapon, damage per shot, armor penetration and magazine size.

name: Expanded Countermeasures Dispenser
desc: Extra flare magazines and a faster dispenser: %s more flares on frigates, %s more on larger ships (normally %s for frigates/destroyers/cruisers/capitals). Flares decoy IR missiles; radar missiles ignore them.

name: IRCCM Package
desc: Hardened seekers for this ship's IR missiles, and its fighters'. They never lose a cold target, and a single flare has at most a %s chance of pulling them off a cold target and almost none off a hot one. Only a heavy blanket of flares (more than %s) still works.

name: Datalink Integration
desc: Shares radar with every other Datalink ship. Linked radars add together, and any linked ship can fire at anything the network is tracking, even with its own radar off.

name: Radar Absorbing Materials
desc: A radar-absorbing coating on the hull. The ship's radar cross section is %s smaller, so enemy radars pick it up %s closer and radar missiles have trouble holding a lock, but the soft coating costs %s of its armor and hull.

name: AESA Radar
desc: Swaps the ship's search radar for an active electronically scanned array. Radar power is %s higher, so it spots targets of every size %s further out. Makes a good radar picket, especially with Datalink Integration.

name: Radar Removal
desc: Rips out the search radar to free up ordnance points. The ship can't detect anything by radar and has no radar scope, and its radar missiles can only launch at targets shared over Datalink Integration. Incompatible with AESA Radar.

name: High-Capacity Shuttles
desc: Stripped-down boarding shuttles that carry %s marines each instead of %s, with %s thinner armor. The space freed up aboard holds %s more marines. Destroyers and larger; needs a Boarding Shuttle Bay. Incompatible with Efficient Boarding Bay.

name: Efficient Boarding Bay
desc: A reorganized boarding bay: %s/%s/%s/%s shuttles per wave by hull size (%s more), and a new wave every %s seconds instead of %s. Destroyers and larger; needs a Boarding Shuttle Bay. Incompatible with High-Capacity Shuttles.

name: Compact Security Forge
desc: Gives up %s of the cargo space to a forge that builds security droids to fight off boarders: %s/%s/%s/%s by hull size, each worth %s of a marine. They never board, take losses before your marines, and are rebuilt over 1 to 3 days after a fight. Not for automated ships.

name: Militia Lockers
desc: Weapon lockers and boarding drills for the whole crew. When the ship is boarded, the crew fight back at %s of a marine's strength instead of %s. Crew killed this way are lost.
short: The crew fight off boarders.

name: Auxiliary Generator
desc: A secondary generator for the power grid: reactor power regenerates %s faster. Incompatible with Backup Generator.
short: Faster power regeneration.

name: Secondary Energy Banks
desc: Extra storage banks for the reactor: %s more power capacity. Incompatible with Backup Generator.
short: More power storage.

name: Backup Generator
desc: A separate generator for the drive. If the reactor melts down the engines keep running, so the ship can still get away; shields and energy weapons stay down until the reactor restarts. Incompatible with Auxiliary Generator and Secondary Energy Banks.
short: Engines keep running after a reactor meltdown.

name: Expanded Propellant
desc: Bigger propellant charges for every ballistic gun. Shells fly %s faster, so they arrive sooner and punch through armor better. The charges take up magazine space: %s fewer rounds, and a magazine cook-off is %s stronger.
short: Faster shells that punch through more armor, but smaller magazines.

name: Blowout Panels
desc: Weak panels above each magazine vent a cook-off away from the hull. The weapon is still lost, but the ship takes %s less of the blast and the chance of a fire is %s lower.
short: Magazine cook-offs do far less damage.

name: Breaching Charges
desc: Boarding shuttles carry shaped charges to blast their way in. Each shuttle that docks deals %s hull damage (never enough to wreck the prize), and this ship's first wave on a target gets %s more attack for %s seconds. Needs a Boarding Shuttle Bay.
short: Boarding shuttles blast their way in.

name: Thermal Dispersal Plating
desc: Conductive layers that spread the heat from energy hits through the armor. Energy bolts heat the armor %s less and hot spots cool %s as fast, but armor is %s lower.
short: Energy weapons heat the armor less.

name: Wet Magazine Stowage
desc: Floods the compartments around every magazine. A shell that gets inside the hull is %s less likely to set off a magazine, and a cook-off is %s less likely to start a fire, but the ship carries %s less ballistic and missile ammo. Stacks with Blowout Panels.
short: Magazines rarely cook off.

name: Passive Sensor Suite (ESM)
desc: Passive receivers that pick up enemy emissions: radars that are on, running jammers, and ECM Packages jamming missiles, out to %s their own range. In RTS mode they show as rough contacts, a dashed circle up to %s of the distance off. These aren't radar tracks, so radar missiles can't launch at them. Works without a radar of its own.
short: Hears enemy radars from far away.

name: Anti-Radiation Missile Conversion
desc: Converts the seekers on this ship's radar missiles into anti-radiation seekers. They launch at and home on any enemy the ship's ESM can hear, with no radar lock needed, and stealth coatings and ECM don't fool them. If the target goes quiet they keep flying straight, and go dumb after %s seconds. Requires a Passive Sensor Suite (ESM).
short: Radar missiles home on enemy emissions.

name: Tandem Warheads
desc: Two-stage warheads on every missile this ship fires: a precursor charge gets through shields and reactive armor, at a cost of %s of the warhead each time. A missile hitting a raised shield spends that much on the shield and the rest hits the hull, and a reactive armor charge only absorbs that share instead of stopping it. After a shield and a charge, nothing is left.
short: Missiles get through shields and reactive armor.

name: Combat Information Center
desc: Makes a capital ship the fleet's command ship. Its early-warning radar reaches %s as far, or %s as far inside a %s-degree cone on sector scan, and it has an ESM suite built in. Sightings from any ship reach the whole fleet within %s seconds instead of up to %s. The antennas make it easier to find on radar, and if it's lost the fleet loses its picture for %s seconds. From its RTS panel it runs electronic warfare on reactor power: scrambling the radars of up to %s enemy ships, barrage jamming, jamming incoming radar missiles and disrupting nearby enemy fire control. With its radar on it also guides friendly radar missiles, extends nearby point defence and directs carriers' fighters. It carries 3 sensor pickets and can fit both a Munitions Resupply Bay and a Repair Tender Bay. Only one per fleet counts.
short: The fleet's command ship: long-range radar, ESM, fast reports and electronic warfare.

name: Auxiliary CIC
desc: A smaller combat information center for cruisers. Its radar reaches %s as far, or %s inside the sector scan cone, it has an ESM suite built in, and sightings reach the fleet within %s seconds. If the fleet's CIC is lost, it takes over after %s seconds. It has the same electronic warfare at shorter range, scrambling 2 enemy radars and jamming fewer missiles at once, and guides missiles, extends point defence and directs fighters over a shorter reach. It carries 2 sensor pickets.
short: A backup command ship: better radar, ESM and faster reports.

name: Automated Repair Unit
desc: Reduces the time required to repair disabled weapons and engines (in combat) by %s. TCO: fires aboard burn out twice as fast and do 40%% less damage, and once per battle the crew patch a destroyed weapon or engine back into service.
short: Increases weapon repair rate in combat.
sModDesc: Reduces repair time to %s, and reduces overload duration by %s.

name: Stabilized Shields
desc: Reduces the amount of soft flux raised shields generate per second by %s. Does not affect the hard flux generated as a result of shields taking damage. TCO: shield hits also draw 40%% less reactor power.
short: Reduces flux upkeep for shields.
sModDesc: Converts %s of the hard flux damage taken by shields to soft flux.
